sentences.text: If you bolt two wings onto a tube, you have an airplane.
But the flat wings give no lift, so the wheels turn and the plane just sits on the runway.
A Cessna 172 weighs about 2,450 pounds, and gravity pins every pound of it down.
So you add an engine and a propeller that push air past the wings, but flat wings let the air slide by.
So you curve the top of the wing, and the air speeds up over it and the wing lifts.
But now the nose wanders, so you add a tail with a fin and stabilizer to keep it pointing straight.
Then you hinge the back of the tail, so the rudder swings the nose sideways and the elevator swings it up.
The curved wing shape is called an airfoil.
At about 100 kilometers per hour, the air over the wings lifts the plane off the runway.
But a gust of wind pushes one wing down, and the plane tips onto its side.
And to land, the plane must slow down, but at 100 kilometers per hour it is far too fast.
So you add flaps on the wings that level the plane and slow it until it settles onto the runway.
And the engine is not what holds a plane up.
The wing does the lifting, so with the engine off a Cessna 172 glides about nine meters forward for every meter it drops.
Add a door, windows and stairs so people can board.
Congratulations, you have built an airplane.
